diagnostic_evidence.quote: $A_\omega$ is defined for any $\omega \in [0,1]$ and is continuous with respect to $\omega$ there.

issues.failure_explanation: Every metric is continuous, so the hypothesis is vacuous. In a general complete metric space the argmin may fail to exist or to be unique, and it need not be continuous in omega. In the two-point discrete space, the argmin is x for omega<1/2 and y for omega>1/2, with a tie at 1/2. Definition item 1 therefore fails.

failure_location.quote: It is easy to verify that if the metric $d$ is continuous as a function of its arguments, then the binary Fr\'echet mean satisfies all the requirements of Definition~\ref{def:average}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to spaces where the binary Fréchet mean exists, is unique and is continuous in omega, for example uniquely geodesic or Hadamard spaces.
issues.overall_effect: The 'canonical example' of an average is not valid in the stated generality.
issues.title: Binary Fréchet mean claimed to be an average in every metric space
issues.why_classification: Peripheral example; restricting its scope loses no main result.

issues.failure_explanation: By the parameter rule, t^{k+1}_{2j+2} lies in [t^k_{j+1}, t^k_{j+2}). Hence [t^{k+1}_{2j}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) is generally not contained in [t^k_j, t^k_{j+1}); for the dual parameterization it strictly overshoots. For t in [t^k_{j+1}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}), the bound d(S^k(P)_j, PA(Q^k;t)) <= delta(S^k(P)) is not justified.

failure_location.quote: which allows us to apply the boundedness property of Definition~\ref{def:average} once more to get

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the triangle inequality through p^k_{j+1} to obtain the bound 2 delta(S^k(P)), and adjust the constant B.
issues.overall_effect: Bound (eqn:bound_term3) is unproven for non-primal parameterizations; the constant in the Cauchy estimate is affected.
issues.title: False interval inclusion used for the third term in the convergence proof
issues.why_classification: A local constant change; the conclusion and rate are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: Contractivity of W is proved only on the set {delta(P) <= nu}, and only for the iterates W^{kL}. Theorem thm:convergence needs contractivity on a W-invariant set, so that delta(W^{kL+r}P) is controlled through delta(W^r P) for 0<r<L. For L>1 nothing bounds delta(W^r P) by nu, or even keeps it finite. D-S controls only the even points, and proximity concerns only S^L versus W^L.

failure_location.quote: Finally, the weak convergence of the scheme $W$ follows by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} since $W$ has a contractivity factor when $\delta(\PP)$ is small enough, it is D-S in $\D$, and it maps $\D$ onto itself.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis such as delta(W(Q)) <= K delta(Q) on D, and shrink the density threshold by K^{L-1} so that every W^r P with r<L stays in {delta <= nu}; or restrict the theorem to L=1.
issues.overall_effect: Weak convergence of W is unsupported for contractivity number L>1, which is advertised as a generalization. The L=1 case, used in cor:added-1, is unaffected.
issues.title: Contractivity of W shown only along multiples of L; invariance needed by Theorem thm:convergence not established
issues.why_classification: Requires an extra hypothesis and a modified threshold, but the result remains comparable.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound ||v-w|| <= d_S(v,w) holds for the Euclidean norm on the Euclidean unit sphere, but not for any norm; it fails for 10 times the Euclidean norm. Lemma hermite_closeness then loses the strict bound ||p~_{2i+-1}-p_i|| < ||p_{i+1}-p_i||, so invariance of D can fail.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the norm in (eqn:metric_hermite) to be Euclidean.
issues.overall_effect: The proximity constant and the invariance of D are unproven for general norms.
issues.title: Chord-arc inequality used with an arbitrary norm
issues.why_classification: A one-line scope fix that keeps every claim used in the application.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and so we do not require $S_1$ to have the D-S property.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses omit D-S for both S_1 and S_2, yet the proof needs it. Counterexample: in R, let S_1=S_2 be the elementary linear scheme plus a translation by 1. It is contractive with mu=1/2 and L=1, D=R^Z is invariant, and proximity holds trivially with distance 0. But S_1^k(P) contains the shift k, so the interpolants diverge.

failure_location.quote: The middle term on the RHS of~\eqref{eqn:W_proof_main} is bounded by $C_{S_1} \delta (S_1^{\ell} (\PP))$ since $S_1$ is D-S.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that S_1 is D-S in D (or S_2 is D-S, with an added proximity term), and delete the claim in rem:prox_2. The scheme (eqn:additional_round) is D-S.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false as stated, and the claim in rem:prox_2 that D-S is not needed is false. Results built on it lose support.
issues.title: Second-type convergence theorem uses D-S of S_1, which is not assumed and is claimed unnecessary
issues.why_classification: Adding a hypothesis restores the theorem but withdraws an advertised feature.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, note that the power of $\eta$ scales like $\cdot/L$ with respect to the number of refinements.

issues.failure_explanation: Proximity of S_1^L to S_2^L bounds the error only at the inputs S_1^{jL}P, with bound E eta^{j+1}, i.e. about eta^{l/L} at level l. The proof uses eta^{l-L+1} at every level l. For L>1 this is unjustified, both in its inputs and in the stronger decay.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply proximity from each starting datum S_1^r P in D, with E' = max_r E(S_1^r P), and use the exponent floor((l-L)/L)+1. The same alpha^{floor(l/L)}(C + 2E' floor(l/L)) bound follows.
issues.overall_effect: Recursion (eqn:delta_S1P) is unproven for L>1, although the final estimate survives with alpha^{floor(l/L)}.
issues.title: Wrong exponent and inputs when invoking proximity of S_1^L to S_2^L
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation gives the same decay and conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, note that the power of $\eta$ scales like $\cdot/L$ with respect to the number of refinements.

issues.failure_explanation: Proximity of S_1^{L_1} to S_2^{L_1} gives an error of order E eta^{l/L_1} at level l, not eta^{l-L_1+1}. Multiplied by 2^l, the divided-difference error is about (2 eta^{1/L_1})^l. This decays only if eta < 2^{-L_1}. For L_1>1 and 2^{-L_1} <= eta < 1/2, for example eta=0.4 and L_1=2, the term grows and alpha=max{2eta,mu_1} is not the right rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require eta < 2^{-L_1} (redefining the order relative to L_1), or restrict to L_1=1, which covers the application in lem:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: The C^1 conclusion is unsupported for first-order contractivity number L_1>1.
issues.title: Order-1 proximity with eta<1/2 does not give decaying divided-difference errors when L_1>1
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the hypothesis; the application survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $S_2$ be a subdivision scheme defined on $\R^n$ that satisfies~\eqref{eqn:contractivity_diff} with a contractivity factor $\mudelta$ and a contractivity number $L_1$

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis controls only scaled second differences. It does not imply that delta contracts: adding a ramp c*i to the outputs of Chaikin's scheme leaves second differences unchanged, but delta(S(P)) >= c for constant P. Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType requires S_2 to be zero-order contractive with the same L, so it is applied outside its hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the convergence of $S_1$ is guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} since $S_2$ is contractive and proximity of order $m=1$ implies proximity of order $m=0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add zero-order contractivity of S_2 with contractivity number L_1 (and D-S) to the hypotheses; these hold in the application.
issues.overall_effect: Convergence of S_1, and hence the C^1 claim, is unsupported under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Zero-order contractivity of S_2 invoked but not assumed
issues.why_classification: Adds a standard hypothesis that the proof already uses; scope and conclusion survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The middle term on the RHS of~\eqref{eqn:W_proof_main} is bounded by $C_{S_1} \delta (S_1^{\ell} (\PP))$ since $S_1$ is D-S.

issues.failure_explanation: Transferring the Cauchy argument to the divided-difference sequences requires a middle-term bound of the form ||(Delta S_1^{l+1}P/2^{-l-1})_{2j} - (Delta S_1^l P/2^{-l})_j|| <= C delta(Delta S_1^l P/2^{-l}). This is D-S for divided differences. Nonlinear S_1 does not induce a scheme on divided differences, and no such estimate is assumed or proved for S_1 or S_2.

failure_location.quote: Thus, the rest of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} is valid for

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a D-S property for the divided differences of S_2 (true for linear S_2). Transfer it to S_1 via the proximity bound 2^{l+1} E eta^{l+1}, which is summable when 2eta<1 and L_1=1, and then run the Cauchy argument.
issues.overall_effect: Convergence of the divided differences, and thus C^1 smoothness, is unproven.
issues.title: No D-S-type estimate for divided differences in the C^1 proof
issues.why_classification: Needs a new hypothesis and a contained argument; the result remains comparable.
